prd_items.note: Statement: the implementation always verifies the target host name (SSLSocket does not), no option turns it off; AC-1/AC-2 make a certificate naming another host fail with 502 CONNECT_FAILED, also with a custom sslSocketFactory.

setEndpointIdentificationAlgorithm("HTTPS") by reflection where it exists (JDK, Android 24+), HttpsURLConnection.getDefaultHostnameVerifier() otherwise (Android < 24). AC-6 now exercises the fallback with the verifier the proxy holds (default getDefaultHostnameVerifier(), test seam injects a recording one); fills: PRD-163/defect is a real gap (JDK default verifier rejects every host: reproduced, DefaultHostnameVerifier.verify("localhost", null)=false on OpenJDK 17.0.20.1) and keeps the item's production behaviour.

AC-A13 clause by clause: no Content-Type + Content-Length: 5 + 5 bytes (FR-HTTP-036 AC-1, FR-ENGINE-014 AC-3, FR-SVL-010 AC-4); HEAD -> Content-Length: 5, no body (FR-HTTP-037 AC-5, FR-ENGINE-014 AC-5, FR-SVL-010 AC-4); 204 -> neither (FR-HTTP-037 AC-6, FR-ENGINE-014 AC-5, FR-SVL-010 AC-4); relay(in,-1) unknown length (FR-HTTP-037 AC-3, FR-ENGINE-014 AC-4); relay(in,-2) IAE (FR-HTTP-037 AC-4); 3-byte stream aborts (FR-HTTP-037 AC-1, FR-ENGINE-014 AC-6); defaultCache adds no Cache-Control (FR-HTTP-036 AC-5). The 304 'client receives Content-Length: 5' clause is narrowed by PRD-271: core commits it (FR-HTTP-037 AC-5), TinyHttpd omits it (FR-ENGINE-014 AC-5), servlet hands it to the container (FR-SVL-010 AC-4). Accepted as narrowed.

Every clause present: relay hands the 304 length to the adapter (FR-HTTP-037 AC-5/AC-9); in-memory adapter delivers it (FR-HTTP-037 AC-5, FR-PROXY-014 AC-5); servlet adapter hands it over (FR-SVL-010 AC-4); TinyHttpd 3.1.1 omits it (FR-ENGINE-014 AC-5, matches ExchangeResponse.commit at e73cd5d and the local de5c7ff checkout); TinyHttpd not changed (FR-ENGINE-014 Rationale note); documented (OPS-DX-009 AC-7). No 0.12.0 criterion still promises a TinyHttpd client a 304 Content-Length.

srs_items.note: Statement keeps the length in what relay commits; AC-5 adds the adapter-dependent client view; AC-9 restricts the 304 length to the committed headers. Consistent with FR-ENGINE-014, FR-SVL-010, FR-PROXY-014, OPS-DX-009.
Testable on the in-memory adapter; client 304 Content-Length delegated to adapters.
Restates expired FR-HTTP-017 AC-1 with the relay exception scoped to committed headers.

evidence.detail: Probe on OpenJDK 17.0.20.1 (scratchpad Probe.java): plain Socket connected to 127.0.0.1, then SSLSocketFactory.getDefault().createSocket(plain, host, port, true).getSSLParameters().getServerNames(): host "localhost" -> null (no SNI extension); host "example.test" -> [type=host_name (0), value=example.test]. AC-3 quote: 'For a target given by host name (for example `https://localhost:<port>`), the SNI server name the https backend receives in the TLS ClientHello is that target host name.'

findings.description: SEC-PROXY-005 AC-3 cannot pass with its own example: the JDK sends no SNI for a single-label host such as localhost, so the mandated createSocket(plain, host, port, true) alone does not deliver 'SNI carries the target host name' (statement, line 1309) for that target.

evidence.detail: docs/spec/06.engine-adapter.srs.md:2071 (Implementation Notes): 'check that TinyHttpd does not add its own `Content-Type` when none is set and keeps a `Content-Length` header on a `HEAD` or `304` response.' vs docs/spec/06.engine-adapter.srs.md:2047 (AC-5): 'answers a `304` response with no body bytes and no `Content-Length` (TinyHttpd 3.1.1 never writes `Content-Length` on a 304 ...)'.

findings.description: The amendment changed AC-5 but left the implementation note asking for a 304 Content-Length over TinyHttpd.

evidence.detail: docs/spec/14.servlet-adapter.srs.md:2058 (Implementation Notes): 'Check that the container neither adds a default `Content-Type` nor strips `Content-Length` from a `HEAD` or `304` response written through `commit`.' vs docs/spec/14.servlet-adapter.srs.md:2032 (AC-4): 'the client seeing `Content-Length: 5` only if the container writes it for a 304 and never another value'.

findings.description: The note treats a container that strips Content-Length from a 304 as something to rule out, while amended AC-4 (PRD-271) accepts it; only the HEAD part of the note still holds.

evidence.detail: Considered OPS-DX-009 AC-4 ('keeps a non-negative length as `Content-Length` without a body for HEAD and 304') against AC-7 (client sees the 304 length only where the adapter writes it).

findings.description: Not a contradiction: AC-4 describes what relay commits (FR-HTTP-037 AC-5/AC-9 use the same wording), AC-7 adds the per-adapter client view.

evidence.detail: Considered FR-HTTP-037 title/statement ('keeps the length on HEAD and 304', 'keeping a non-negative length as Content-Length for HEAD and 304') against AC-5 adapter clause.

findings.description: Not a contradiction: the statement is about the core's committed headers; AC-5/AC-9 say so explicitly and FR-PROXY-014 notes use the same reading.
